{{1964 Summer Olympics}}

The [[1964 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the XVIII Olympiad, and commonly known as Tokyo 1964, were an international [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Tokyo]], Japan, from 9 to 24 October.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 {{!}} Olympic Games |url=https://olympics.com/en/sport-events/tokyo-1964 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240217204527/https://olympics.com/en/sport-events/tokyo-1964 |archive-date=17 February 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=22 July 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964: A golden legacy |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/tokyo-1964-playback-first-asian-olympics-legacy-infrastructure-technology |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=10 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228073752/https://olympics.com/en/news/tokyo-1964-playback-first-asian-olympics-legacy-infrastructure-technology |archive-date=28 February 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Kano |first1=Shintaro |access-date=22 July 2024 }}</ref> A total of 5,151 athletes representing 93 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 Summer Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240613221907/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964 |archive-date=13 June 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=22 July 2024 }}</ref> The games featured 163 events across 19 [[Olympic sports|sports]] and 24 disciplines.<ref>{{cite web |title=1964: Tokyo, Japan |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.720/1964-tokyo-japan-1.1139012 |website=[[CBC Sports]] | access-date=25 July 2024 |date=15 June 2012 |archive-date=30 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730124258/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.720/1964-tokyo-japan-1.1139012 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Olympedia – 1964 Summer Olympics Overview |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/16 |website=[[Olympedia]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715232526/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/16 |archive-date=15 July 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> Two new sports were introduced to the [[Summer Olympic Games]] program in Tokyo: judo and volleyball.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964: The First Chapter |url=https://www.ijf.org/news/show/tokyo-1964-the-first-chapter |website=[[International Judo Federation]] | date=8 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231127100527/https://www.ijf.org/news/show/tokyo-1964-the-first-chapter |archive-date=27 November 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Messer |first1=Nicolas |access-date=22 July 2024 |language=en }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=History of volleyball: From humble beginnings to a global sport |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/what-history-volleyball-game-origin-mintonette-ymca-fivb-olympics |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=5 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106152723/https://olympics.com/en/news/what-history-volleyball-game-origin-mintonette-ymca-fivb-olympics |archive-date=6 January 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Peter |first1=Naveen |access-date=22 July 2024 }}</ref> The inclusion of volleyball marked the first time that a women's team sport had been introduced.<ref>{{cite web |title=The History of Olympic Volleyball |url=https://avp.com/news/olympic-history-volleyball/ |website=[[Association of Volleyball Professionals]] | date=18 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808174515/https://avp.com/news/olympic-history-volleyball/ |archive-date=8 August 2020 |url-status=live |access-date=22 July 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Volleyball at Tokyo 1964 |url=https://olympics.com/en/video/volleyball-at-tokyo-1964 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228073534/https://olympics.com/en/video/volleyball-at-tokyo-1964 |archive-date=28 February 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=22 July 2024 }}</ref>

The 1964 Summer Games were the first Olympics held in Asia,<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 |url=https://olympic.ca/games/1964-tokyo/ |website=[[Canadian Olympic Committee]] | date=10 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413161652/https://olympic.ca/games/1964-tokyo/ |archive-date=13 April 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> and marked the first time [[Apartheid-era South Africa and the Olympics|South Africa was excluded]] for using its [[Apartheid|apartheid system]] in sports.<ref>{{cite web |title=1964: South Africa banned from Olympics |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/august/18/newsid_3547000/3547872.stm |website=[[BBC News]] | date=18 August 1964 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231206030930/http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/august/18/newsid_3547000/3547872.stm |archive-date=6 December 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Find Out Why South Africa Was Barred From the Olympics for 32 Years |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/why-south-africa-barred-from-the-olympics-apartheid |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=26 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228073307/https://olympics.com/en/news/why-south-africa-barred-from-the-olympics-apartheid |archive-date=28 February 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> [[North Korea at the Olympics|North Korea]] and [[Indonesia at the Olympics|Indonesia]] withdrew their athletes from the 1964 Summer Olympics just before the games were due to start, as the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) were refusing to accept any athletes who had participated in the [[GANEFO|Games of the New Emerging Forces]] held in [[Jakarta]], Indonesia, in 1963.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 Olympic Games {{!}} History, Highlights, Legacy, & Summer Olympics |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/Tokyo-1964-Olympic-Games |website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205230533/https://www.britannica.com/event/Tokyo-1964-Olympic-Games |archive-date=5 December 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 |language=en }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 October 1964 |title=3 Countries Withdraw From Olympics; North Korea Out Over Suspension; Indonesia Also Quits Games Because of Ban—Internal Strife Sidelines Ecuador |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1964/10/09/archives/3-countries-withdraw-from-olympics-north-korea-out-over-suspension.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725183558/https://www.nytimes.com/1964/10/09/archives/3-countries-withdraw-from-olympics-north-korea-out-over-suspension.html |archive-date=25 July 2024 |access-date=25 July 2024 |website=[[The New York Times]] | page=52 }}</ref> [[China at the Olympics|China]] continued their boycott of the games, which began in 1952 and lasted until 1984, over the participation of [[Chinese Taipei at the Olympics|Taiwan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What, exactly, is a 'diplomatic boycott' of the Beijing Olympics? |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/32831100/what-exactly-diplomatic-boycott-beijing-olympics |website=[[ESPN]] | date=10 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240702091939/https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/32831100/what-exactly-diplomatic-boycott-beijing-olympics |archive-date=2 July 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Hamilton |first1=Tom |access-date=25 July 2024 |language=en }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic bans and boycotts go back a century |url=https://apnews.com/article/taiwan-winter-olympics-politics-sports-protests-and-demonstrations-8808adcab94bcc3eedc1fdd2fd8441a0 |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=2023-02-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616235458/https://apnews.com/article/taiwan-winter-olympics-politics-sports-protests-and-demonstrations-8808adcab94bcc3eedc1fdd2fd8441a0 |archive-date=2024-06-16 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

Overall, 41 teams received at least one medal, with 26 of them winning at least one gold medal. Athletes from the [[Soviet Union at the 1964 Summer Olympics|Soviet Union]] won the most medals overall, with 96, while the [[United States at the 1964 Summer Olympics|United States]] won the most gold medals, with 36.<ref name="medal count" /> The [[Bahamas at the 1964 Summer Olympics|Bahamas]] won their first gold medal ever, doing so in the [[Sailing at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Star|star class sailing event]],<ref>{{cite web |title=The Bahamas – and the Olympic Movement – honour the late Sir Durward Knowles, centenarian and Olympian extraordinaire |url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1062362/the-bahamas-and-the-olympic-movement-honour-sir-durward-knowles-centenarian-and-olympian-extraordinaire |website=[[Inside the Games]] | date=8 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220501223804/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1062362/the-bahamas-and-the-olympic-movement-honour-sir-durward-knowles-centenarian-and-olympian-extraordinaire |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-status=live |last1=Rowbottom |first1=Mike |access-date=23 July 2024 }}</ref> while athletes from [[Kenya at the 1964 Summer Olympics|Kenya]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Kenya's first Olympic medalist dies aged 84 |url=https://www.africanews.com/2022/11/02/kenyas-first-olympic-medalist-dies-aged-84// |website=[[Africanews]] | date=2 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240304012626/https://www.africanews.com/2022/11/02/kenyas-first-olympic-medalist-dies-aged-84/ |archive-date=4 March 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 |language=en }}</ref> [[Nigeria at the 1964 Summer Olympics|Nigeria]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=History of Nigeria at the Olympic Games since 1952 |url=https://www.premiumtimesng.com/sports/nigeria-sports-news/474685-history-of-nigeria-at-the-olympic-games-since-1952.html?tztc=1 |newspaper=[[Premium Times]] | date=20 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725035853/https://www.premiumtimesng.com/sports/nigeria-sports-news/474685-history-of-nigeria-at-the-olympic-games-since-1952.html?tztc=1 |archive-date=25 July 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Alaka |first1=Jide |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> and [[Tunisia at the 1964 Summer Olympics|Tunisia]] won their nations' first Olympic medals of any kind.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mohamed Gammoudi |url=https://www.70yearsmg.com/athletes/mohamed-gammoudi/ |website=[[International Committee of Mediterranean Games]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207222059/https://www.70yearsmg.com/athletes/mohamed-gammoudi/ |archive-date=7 December 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref>

Soviet gymnast [[Larisa Latynina]] won the most medals at the games with six (two gold, two silver, and two bronze).<ref>{{cite web |title=1964 Tokyo Summer Games {{!}} Olympics |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1964/ |website=[[Sports Reference]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114073426/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1964/ |archive-date=14 January 2020 |url-status=dead |access-date=25 July 2024}}</ref> With 18 total Olympic medals, Latynina became the world record holder for [[List of multiple Olympic medalists|most Olympic medals won by an individual]], a record that stood for 48 years until swimmer [[Michael Phelps]] surpassed that mark at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 July 2012 |title=Edoardo Mangiarotti |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/edoardo-mangiarotti-5dncnt7qv3b |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730122806/https://www.thetimes.com/article/edoardo-mangiarotti-5dncnt7qv3b |archive-date=30 July 2024 |access-date=30 July 2024 |website=[[The Times]] | language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Olympics: A visual guide to the history and story of the Games |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/extra/xawtd9l5mx/visual-guide-to-the-olympics |website=[[BBC Sport]] | access-date=25 July 2024 |archive-date=30 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730124403/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/extra/xawtd9l5mx/visual-guide-to-the-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref> She also became the record holder for most gold and total Olympic medals by a female athlete.<ref>{{cite web |title=Who has the most Olympic medals? The countries and athletes with the most wins of all time |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/2024-paris-games-most-olympic-medals-ever |website=[[CBS News]] | date=25 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240729123926/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/2024-paris-games-most-olympic-medals-ever/ |archive-date=29 July 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Chasan |first1=Aliza |access-date=25 July 2024}}</ref>

== Medal table ==

The medal table is based on information provided by the IOC and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] | date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us}}</ref>

At the 1964 Summer Olympics, athletes were tied in three events, all of which were gymnastics events. In the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Men's artistic individual all-around|men's artistic individual all-around]] event there was a three-way tie for second, which resulted in three silver medals and no bronze medal being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 individual all-round men Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964/results/gymnastics-artistic/individual-all-round-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | access-date=24 July 2024 |archive-date=21 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121224320/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964/results/gymnastics-artistic/individual-all-round-men |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Men's floor|men's floor]] event, two silver medals and no bronze medal were awarded due to a tie.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 vault women Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964/results/gymnastics-artistic/vault-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | access-date=24 July 2024 |archive-date=22 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122010840/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964/results/gymnastics-artistic/vault-women |url-status=live }}</ref> Lastly, in the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Women's vault|women's vault]] event, two silver medals and no bronze medal were awarded due to a tie.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tokyo 1964 floor exercises men Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964/results/gymnastics-artistic/floor-exercises-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121223401/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-1964/results/gymnastics-artistic/floor-exercises-men |archive-date=21 November 2021 |url-status=live |access-date=24 July 2024 }}</ref>
